purpose: Five-backend actor subtree quotas for registered native handles and trusted accounted bytes
ownership: Only trusted native host adapters mint registration and retirement receipts. Guest labels cannot forge identity.
contract: Quota boundaries: process/context cap and immutable actor-permission ancestor caps all apply (intersection).
Registered native resources charge each permission-scope ancestor until host-owned physical close or explicitly trusted unregister ownership transfer.
Outstanding physical loans defer unregister transfer completion and quota refund until last loan leaves.
Logical actor STOP/revocation does not refund existing registered-resource credits. New admission must fail against exact actor incarnation.
Accounted bytes are trusted host declarations, not actual heap/OS measurement. Unknown-byte registrations still consume one handle.
Native handle creation before registration can exceed a post-registration limit. Trusted brokers must pre-reserve OS creation credits for hard enforcement.
Post-shutdown late resource publication is rejected but retained/quarantined until physical resource closure; no false clean retirement.
Failed close retains registered resources and actor liveness until retry or quarantine.
Actor/native context shutdown requires bounded repeated physical joins; never report a stop before resource retirement.
